saints.name: St. Lucy
saints.title: Virgin and Martyr
saints.shortBlurb: A virgin martyr of Syracuse in the persecution of Diocletian, honored as a bringer of light in the dark of winter…
biography: Born about 283 into a wealthy family of Syracuse in Sicily, Lucy had secretly vowed her virginity to God. When her mother Eutychia was healed of a long issue of blood after prayer at the tomb of Agatha at Catania, Lucy won her consent to refuse marriage and to give her dowry to the poor.

Her rejected suitor denounced her as a Christian to the governor Paschasius in the persecution of Diocletian. Sentenced to be dragged away to dishonor, she could not be moved, even by a team of oxen; the fire kindled around her did not burn her; and at length she perished by the sword, about the year 304.

Her very name, from the Latin lux, means light; and her feast, falling in the old calendar near the shortest day, made her the light-bearer of the North, where maidens still wear crowns of candles on her morning. From her name, and from the later legend of her eyes, she is invoked as patroness of the blind and of all with diseases of the eye. Her name stands in the Roman Canon of the Mass.
saints.knownFor: Her virgin martyrdom; patroness of the blind and of light.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 13 December
